commands.magicrpg.export.dimension: Run this command in Goldenwood, the Lilac Meadows, the Iron Wastelands, or the Storm Reefs.
commands.magicrpg.export.area: The extra area must be within 524,288 blocks of the origin on each axis and cover at most %s chunks.
commands.magicrpg.export.failure: Could not export the island map to %s. See the server log.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_ASH_HOUND.1:
At my Arcane Worktable I bound coal, bone and gunpowder into a Summoning Seal. It flared when I touched it to the top of a solid block. I had left two blocks of clear space above it, and there the hound appeared.
It crouched, growled and shed sparks. I stepped aside as it lunged and struck while it recovered. A Charred Fang lay in the ashes.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_CHARRED_FANG.1: The fang I picked up after fighting the Ash Hound held its heat even in the cold ashes. An arch of Arcane Stone Bricks opened onto the Lilac Meadows, an amber one led to Goldenwood, and an iron one showed me a city under ash. When I held it against Dark Prismarine, I heard the surf. Each arch consumed one fang. I have written down how I built the frame for each world.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_STORM_REEFS: Where stone holds back the sea
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_STORM_REEFS.1:
The Charred Fang sparked against Dark Prismarine, and I heard waves breaking. I built a frame from fourteen blocks of Dark Prismarine with an opening two blocks wide and three tall. When I touched the fang to the frame, it burned away. The veil swallowed the water in the opening, and a lighthouse appeared through the arch.
The island arch took me back to my entrance. Once, magic carried me to the reefs by another route. I lit the arch on the breakwater with a fang, and it took me to the world's spawn point.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_STORM_REEFS.2: I spotted two side paths from the breakwater. A broken mast jutted out of the water by the western path. I found a bell in a chest among the timbers below deck. When I reached the eastern signal tower, I found a spare bell in a barrel beside the cartography table.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_STORM_PILOT: A bell in the lighthouse circle
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_STORM_PILOT.1:
My bell hummed outside the lighthouse. I touched it to the Lodestone between the sea lanterns. The bell crumbled, and the Storm Pilot rose from the center of the circle.
Ten minutes after I defeated it, I saw it rise over the same tiles. For the first summons, I made the bell at a crafting table from two copper ingots, an amethyst shard, and a prismarine crystal.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_STORM_PILOT.2:
My Thaumostatic Harness went quiet as the Pilot turned on me. I stepped aside when sparks traced a lane across the tiles and leapt over the low wave.
As the Pilot weakened, it closed its copper fins and blue flames marked the outer ring. I took shelter in the center. After the discharge the fins opened, and my blows left deeper cracks in the exposed shell.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_REEFHEART.1: I found a warm lens and prismarine crystals among the Pilot’s remains. I squeezed the lens before diving and could breathe underwater and swim faster for half a minute. My companions within six paces felt it too. After a minute the heart responded to my touch again.
item.magicrpg.storm_bell.altar: The Storm Bell responds to the Lodestone in the lighthouse circle on the Storm Reefs.
item.magicrpg.storm_bell.peaceful: Set the difficulty to Easy or higher to summon the Storm Pilot.
item.magicrpg.storm_bell.busy: The Storm Pilot is already in the arena.
item.magicrpg.storm_bell.returning: The Storm Pilot is still gathering its strength.
item.magicrpg.storm_bell.blocked: Clear the center of the circle and try summoning again.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.storm_reefs_f: The fang needs a complete Dark Prismarine frame with a 2×3 opening.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.storm_reefs_n: Check the return arch's frame and landing on the Storm Reefs.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.already_open: The portal is already open. Step through the opening.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.opening_block: The veil could not hold inside the frame.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.protected: You need permission to change blocks here to open this portal.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.wrong_return_: Use the return arch at the island landing.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.destination_u: The destination is unavailable. Check that the dimension is loaded on the server.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_IRON_WASTELAND:
The fang hissed against the iron as if I had thrown it into a forge. I built the frame from fourteen Iron Blocks with an opening two blocks wide and three tall. The fang burned away when I touched it to the iron. The veil swallowed the bricks I had stacked in the opening, and a street took shape beneath a gray sky.
On my way back I used the arch where I had arrived. It brought me to the frame I had entered through.

From the threshold I saw an iron head the size of a house lying in the dust. Beyond it, the avenue led to a foundry and two bridges crossed the rift toward the factory chimneys. From an intact floor of the western tower I made out colossi on the move.
I pried Iron Rubble and Metal Plates from the road. Ashen Soil lay underneath, and rust crusted the old iron supports.

I found traces of old seals in the foundry. From them I pieced together the original command. When a magical plague began turning townsfolk into monsters, the smiths cast iron giants to protect those still alive.
The ruins tell the rest. The colossi broke free, brought down the houses, and destroyed the people they were made to guard. Centuries have passed and they are still fighting the infected in the streets.

I counted eight blocks from the paving to the crown of the Iron Colossus. The chain on its shoulder shifted as it drew one arm aside. I stepped clear just in time, and I saw the next blow drive even a Flesh Titan back. When I brought down a colossus myself, I recovered several dozen iron ingots from its shell.

I recognized the city's former residents by the remnants of their clothes. The Hollowed wandered in small groups, and I saw a colossus bring one down with a single blow.
I spotted a zombie in a thaumaturge's robes among them. It caught up with me well ahead of the others.

By the foundry I saw a Flesh Titan five blocks tall. It stopped a colossus in the middle of the avenue. Both came after me when I drew close. I returned to the fallen colossus after their fight and found no iron ingots.

Beneath the awnings of the empty market I spotted an iron golem nearly twice the height of those that guard villages. It threw one of the infected aside and let a colossus walk past. When it turned toward me, I made for the end of the street.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.iron_wastelan: A complete iron block frame with a 2×3 opening is required.
Check the return arch's frame and landing in the Iron Wastelands.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_LILAC_MEADOWS: A path through the white ridges
I built a frame from 14 Arcane Stone Bricks with an opening two blocks wide and three tall. The Charred Fang burned away when I touched it to a brick, and the lilac veil swallowed the stones I had stacked in the opening.
On the far side I found an ancient arch hung with pennants. I entered from a different arch the next day and came out in the same place. When I stepped back through, the Meadow arch took me to the doorway I had used that day.

I found lilac saplings in the grass beside the arch. One took root in ordinary soil and spread a pink canopy with hanging sprays of leaves. A handful of bone meal hastened its growth. I hung a gold-marked pennant on a wall beneath the tree, then set an ancient crystal cluster on the stone beside it. Its violet light lasted through the night.

I saw purple crystals above the pond as soon as I stepped through my return arch. I followed the white ridge west and found an observatory at the cliff edge. Its chest held a Star Prism. Back at the pond, white steps led me to a balcony over the buried city.

I followed the lit channels and found a Resonance Coil in the eastern workshop. Two pairs of stairs lead to the archive in the west and the crystal hall in the east. Between the houses below the galleries I found two stairways into a crypt. Sarcophagi flank its aisle, and a chest still stands at the far end.
I saw guards gather again around iron cages. While the cages stand, a room I cleared soon fills with footsteps.

The Paladin drew his blade back to his hip and turned his shoulders. I stepped beyond the golden arc and the blade swept past me. When he raised the sword over his helm, a narrow band lit up across the floor. I stepped aside and struck at the exposed joints while he stooped to pull the point free.
As the fight wore on, the core in his chest began to hum. The Paladin lifted the hilt to his visor and drove the point into the floor. I ran beyond the lilac circle and waited for the wave to reach its edge. When I rushed back, he was still bent over his sword.

tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_ANCIENT_MERCHA: Lilac armor of the buried city
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_ANCIENT_MERCHA:
I found a merchant's mark on an old map of the Meadows and traced it onto paper at my Arcane Worktable. I pressed the seal to the top of a solid block with two blocks of space above it. The merchant appeared and the seal crumbled.
I tried it again at home, far from the Meadows, and the merchant stayed there. When I needed a second merchant, I made another seal.

I brought Chalk Hearts from the guardians and Echo Rivets from the Hollow Armor. The merchant sells each piece separately. Here is what he asks in hearts and rivets:

Helmet — 6 and 8.
Chestplate — 8 and 10.
Leggings — 6 and 8.
Boots — 4 and 6.

I put on all four pieces and counted four armor points. My wounds closed as quickly as they did under Regeneration IV. I call it Lilac Restoration. It stopped as soon as I took off one piece.
If I find something that reduces every blow to a scratch, these plates might heal it before the next one lands.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_ARMOR_POUCH: A change of armor in one motion
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_ARMOR_POUCH.1: I divided the pouch into four pockets for a helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots. I hold the pouch and crouch while right-clicking to look inside. Each pocket holds one item I can wear in the matching slot. I even fitted an Elytra in the chest pocket.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_ARMOR_POUCH.2: I right-clicked and the items in the pouch traded places with the ones I wore. An empty pocket took a piece of armor and left its equipment slot bare. My enchantments and signs of wear survived the swap. When a curse kept me from removing my helmet, the whole set stayed on me.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.meadow_no_spa: Check the ancient arch's frame and landing in the Lilac Meadows.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_INVENTORY_SCAN: Aspects at the bottom of my pack
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_INVENTORY_SCAN:
At camp I picked up my Thaumometer with the cursor and held it over a specimen in my pack for about a second. A click told me the reading was recorded. The lens worked just as well over an item in an open chest.
The lens reveals aspects I know and those whose parts I have already encountered. After the click the aspect symbols and their amounts appeared above the specimen. Later I could see them again by hovering with the Thaumometer or by holding Shift while pointing at the item.

At the supply shelves, I held the Thaumometer over an item in the catalogue in the same way. The lens marked the moment the reading went into my notes.
item.magicrpg.ash_hound_seal.space: There is too little room to summon an Ash Hound here.
item.magicrpg.ash_hound_seal.surface: The seal needs a solid surface you can interact with.
item.magicrpg.ash_hound_seal.peaceful: The seal cannot summon an Ash Hound in Peaceful mode.
item.magicrpg.ash_hound_seal.failed: The seal failed to summon an Ash Hound.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.portal_frame: A complete arcane stone brick frame with a 2×3 opening is required.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_WOODEN_DOORS.1: I carved a tree into pale silverwood and a spiral into dark greatwood. At my workbench, six planks of either wood arranged in two columns gave me three doors. Both swung open by hand, and a redstone signal worked the hinges just as well.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.goldenwood_fr: The fang stirs only in a complete amber block frame with a 2×3 opening.
item.magicrpg.charred_fang.goldenwood_no: The return arch has no safe exit, or there is no room to build it on the Goldenwood terrace.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_GOLDENWOOD_ENT:
The hound’s fang warmed when I touched it to amber. I set fourteen solid amber blocks in a four-by-five upright frame, corners included. The frame took a fang, and a golden veil filled the two-by-three opening, swallowing the planks I had stacked there. An incomplete frame took nothing. The fang stayed in my hand when I blocked every safe exit on the terrace, too.

I found a second arch on a stone terrace beyond it. I can cross either veil again without a fang. When my first arch was broken, the second led me to safe ground. Later I took down the return frame. Its stone crumbled, and my next crossing rebuilt the frame in the same spot.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_GOLDENWOOD_INH: Field notes in the fading light
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_GOLDENWOOD_INH:
A bush by the ruins began to tremble. I stepped aside as a sprout ent tore its roots free and lunged. Where it fell, I found golden resin clinging to a chip of bark.

I flushed a brood of amber bark beetles from a rotten log. I drew them into the open before fighting and recovered curved teal plates edged in copper.

I backed away when the guardian lifted its boughs, then struck as it recovered. Deep in the wood I found a crimson knot inside an amber rim.

In a spire a ruin spark flashed violet just before firing. A pillar stopped the bolt. I picked up a violet core shard with a pale seam still running through it.

I followed the blue glimmer of honey moths along the shallows. When a honeybell shone green, I brushed off its pollen with an empty hand. A moth can visit the flower again. In a hamlet I found a pearly wing scale like those the moths leave when killed.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_AMBER_BOW: A bowstring that remembers amber bonds
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_AMBER_BOW.1:
My Elytra lost their lift as I fought the Amber Archer in the fortress courtyard. After I defeated him, I picked up a piece of his bow. Ten minutes later he was back at his post.
I placed the fragment on the central pedestal of my infusion altar and laid goldenwood planks, string, and golden resin around it. After the infusion, I drew the bow again and again without seeing a single crack.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_AMBER_BOW.2: I loosed an ordinary arrow and watched amber sparks hold my target in place for three seconds. Even wings offered no escape. I swung the bow in my main hand (left click) and brought nine arrows down on the nearest enemy within seven blocks. I drew nothing from my quiver for the volley and could call it down again a second later.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_GOLDENWOOD_RUI:
I took the western trail through the hamlet to a ruined fortress. Steps still climbed the tower wall to a chest at the top. Through the east gate I reached a rootbound altar. I found carapace plates and wing scales in the hamlet’s barrels and pollen at the altar.

Beyond the wooden bridge, I followed the road up to a castle with copper roofs. A chest stood on the dais in the great hall. From the north gate I crossed a stone bridge back to the goldenwood.

Beyond the wooden bridge I took the riverside trail. At the falls a stone stair led under the rim of the island to a sunken sanctuary. I followed a side aisle behind the inner wall and found an amber heart in the chest. I climbed back up the same stair.

In the ruined fortress courtyard I heard a crack and felt amber roots close around my boots. I turned toward the archer and raised my shield. The first arrow split the boards, and the second shattered the shield. After the third arrow, the bonds crumbled and the keeper lowered his bow. I reached him in that brief lull.

When he loosed an arrow into the sky, I stepped into a gap between the golden circles. When he turned the bow sideways, I darted aside and the fan of arrows swept past. I pulled an amber heart from beneath his shattered plates.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_GOLDENWOOD_MAT: I split one pale goldenwood log into four planks. Just beneath the amber turf I quarried honeystone with a pickaxe. Four pieces fitted into a square gave me four bricks the colour of honey.
I set a mundane ring beneath my runic matrix. Around it I placed an amber heart, golden resin, a carapace plate, a core shard, glowing pollen and a honey moth scale. I fed the matrix 24 Ignis, 20 Potentia, 16 Fames and 12 Praecantatio. The rite had instability 5. I arranged the six pedestals in opposing pairs.

I slipped the ring into a ring slot and struck the same foe repeatedly in melee. Each landed hit added 12% to the next, up to 60%. After four seconds without wounding that foe, after wounding another, or when I took off the ring, the heat faded.

I touched the matrix with my bare hand. The reading showed me where I had left blocks and items on pedestals without a partner. After I set candles in opposing pairs, the reading rose. A positive number tells me how much the altar offsets the rite’s instability.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_GOLDENWOOD_ENT: I took the white veil below the terrace for mist until I saw the river fall straight through it. The whole wood hangs above the clouds. I followed the lanterns north and found myself beneath the shining crown of a vast goldenwood. I cut a sprig with shears, and the leaves still shone in my study.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_WAYFARER_MIRRO: A road on the other side of the glass
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_WAYFARER_MIRRO: A scrap of mirrored glass shimmered when I laid it on white stone from the Lilac Meadows. On my arcane workbench I put one white stone, one mirrored glass and one dye in any slots. My wand gave 8 Ordo and 4 Aer, and I lifted out two mirrors already bound to each other. The dye colored both frames. A second casting with the same dye made a separate pair.

I hung one mirror on the side of a solid wall and carried its twin to another dimension. I left a firm floor and room to stand in front of both. I stepped into the glass from the front and came out facing away from its twin. Either mirror takes me back without drawing any vis.
When I broke one mirror and hung it elsewhere, the other found it again. With the twin in my pack or the landing blocked, the glass let me go no farther.
The Paladin fell, and I recovered an Oath Core from his armor. Ten minutes later I saw him at his old post. Stone formed under his boots and the obstructions above it crumbled.
I found a City Seal in the chest to the right of the gate, with the stairs to the meadow beyond it. The core answered the prism with a low hum. I wondered what would happen if I brought them together over the infusion altar.
item.magicrpg.time_turner.needs_vis: I need a wand in my other hand with 10 vis of each primal aspect.
item.magicrpg.time_turner.busy: The Time-Turner cannot take hold while time is already disturbed.
item.magicrpg.time_turner.warning.3: Did you hear the clocks catch their breath, %s?
item.magicrpg.time_turner.warning.4: Tread lightly through these stolen seconds, %s.
tc.research_text.MAGICRPG_TIME_TURNER: Thirty seconds in the span of ten
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_TIME_TURNER.1: My clock gained a beat whenever I laid the Star Prism against the Oath Core. I set the core at the heart of my infusion altar and laid out the prism, the clock and the rest of the meadow relics around it. The coil fell silent when the infusion finished. Then every clock in the room struck at once.
tc.research_page.MAGICRPG_TIME_TURNER.2: I held the Time-Turner in my main hand and turned it with my wand in the other. It drew ten vis from each of the six primal aspects. For ten seconds by my own pulse, the world ran three times as fast. Even my companions in other dimensions heard a warning. I had to wait for the world to settle before I could turn it again.
